en: Context is the part that makes up your
context window, of course, but in general,
it's the text, the information you're
sending to an AI model to produce an answer.
And it's a broad variety of things
therefore. It's of course the text you're
sending to a model, but it's also, for
example, the contents of a file you may be
sending to a model, which if you think about
it, is also just text you're sending to the
model. It's also invisible context like
system instructions or maybe developer
instructions if you're using some developer
AI tool.
It's of course the entire conversation
history, so also text you sent in the past
potentially.
It is maybe documents the model retrieved on
its own if you're using some agent, if
you're using Claude Cowork, if you're using
ChatGPT or Claude on your system and it
searches your file system,
the files it found, the list of files it
found, files it found and the content of
some of those files, that goes into the
context. It may be some memory it saved. It
may be tool definitions. If you're using an
AI agent that exposes tools to a model,
something we'll also get back to, the
definitions of these tools, the descriptions
of the tools the model may use, that's also
context that is sent to it.
So it really is the combination of all the
information that matters for a certain task
that is sent to a model to get that model to
produce meaningful output. And it is that
entirety of context that also makes up the
so-called context window.
